children: , the enterprise-server and infrastructure company, added Axelera AI's Europa processor to selected systems as the European startup pushed deeper into data-center inference, Reuters reported Tuesday. Dell shares climbed approximately 3.9% to $585.22 Thursday. The valuation picture is much hotter: GuruFocus shows Dell trading 155.43% above its GF Value estimate of $229.11.

Europa is designed to squeeze substantial AI compute into a relatively lean power envelope. The processor delivers a published 629 trillion operations per second at 45 watts, translating to roughly 14 TOPS per watt. Axelera says more than 600 customers already use its products, while Dell is working with the company on European Union-backed computing projects in Italy and Luxembourg.

The bigger question is how much of that technology pipeline ultimately turns into meaningful Dell revenue. Axelera is pursuing $1.5 billion of potential sales, but management has made clear that figure does not represent booked orders or recognized revenue. For Dell, the immediate benefit is broader AI-infrastructure choice: a power-efficient accelerator could sharpen system economics for inference workloads that do not need premium GPUs. But with the stock already far above its GF Value estimate, investors are paying a steep price for that growth optionality.

title: Dell Gains Nearly 4% Today as 45-Watt Inference Expands Its Server Menu
